title: Myth: Space Makes Perfect Optical Fibre
description: Glass fibre made in orbit sounds ideal, but IEEE Spectrum reports the best gain from microgravity so far is about a two-fold loss reduction against a theoretical hundred-fold, and impurities remain a problem. About 11.9 km was drawn on the ISS (NASA).

beats.text: Is space the secret to perfect fibre?
beats.vo: Glass fibre made in orbit sounds perfect. Is it?

points: Best gain so far: about two times
beats.vo: In space, a fluoride glass called Z B L A N forms fewer crystals, and about eleven kilometres of fibre were drawn on the station. But the best loss reduction is about two times, against a hundred times in theory. Impurities still limit it.

caption:
Myth: space makes perfect optical fibre. 🛰️
Fact: ZBLAN glass forms fewer crystals in orbit, and ~11.9 km was drawn on the ISS — but the best loss cut so far is ~2×, versus ~100× in theory. Impurities and cost remain the limits.
